title: Ibrahimovic Slams Paredes Over World Cup Final Brawl as FIFA Opens Investigation
excerpt: Former Sweden striker says he would have 'headbutted' the Argentine midfielder, while FIFA appoints a prosecutor to probe the ugly post-match scenes at MetLife Stadium.
body:
• Zlatan Ibrahimovic called Leandro Paredes' post-match behavior "unprofessional" and said he would have headbutted the midfielder had he been on the pitch.
  • Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground after Spain's 1-0 World Cup final victory over Argentina at MetLife Stadium.
  • FIFA has appointed a disciplinary prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of its code following the brawl, with multiple Argentine players and staff under scrutiny.
  • Gavi has urged leniency for the Argentine players, saying he does not believe they should be sanctioned.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic tore into Leandro Paredes during his Fox Sports punditry stint on Monday, condemning the Argentine midfielder's violent conduct after Spain's World Cup final victory and drawing a parallel to one of football's most infamous moments.

"Paredes can be happy there was no player like me on the pitch. If I had been there, I would have headbutted him and been sent off. It is unprofessional behaviour from him," Ibrahimovic said, in comments reported by Spanish outlet A.S.

"I don't know what the Spanish players are doing? They are just watching another player hit their team-mate."

— Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Fox Sports pundit

The remark evoked memories of Zinedine Zidane's headbutt on Marco Materazzi in the 2006 World Cup final — a comparison French Football Weekly was quick to highlight, calling the incident "the remake of Zidane-Materazzi."

What Happened After the Final Whistle

Spain lifted the trophy at MetLife Stadium on Sunday after Ferran Torres scored the only goal in the 106th minute of extra time, nodding home from close range after Nico Williams headed the ball into his path. Argentina, already reduced to 10 men following Enzo Fernandez's second-half red card, failed to register a single shot on target across 120 minutes.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=0r19QoB9LKY

Within seconds of the final whistle, the match descended into chaos. Broadcast footage showed Nahuel Molina throwing a punch at Spain captain Rodri as the Spaniards began their celebrations. When Eric Garcia stepped in to intervene, Paredes grabbed the defender by the throat and knocked him to the ground. He and Thiago Almada then wrestled Gavi — who had come onto the pitch as a substitute — to the turf, with what TNT Sports' Alan Shearer described as "two or three haymakers."

Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala was also captured on video appearing to punch Spain's Dani Olmo during the melee. Players and staff from both sides eventually separated the groups.

FIFA Launches Formal Probe

FIFA initially showed Paredes a red card on its official match tracker, but the governing body later confirmed the card had been deleted — attributed to a system error rather than a deliberate decision, according to USA Today.

On Monday, FIFA announced it had appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor under Article 36 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code to investigate the post-match incidents. "Further details will be communicated by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee once the prosecutor's report has been completed," the statement read.

The probe could lead to suspensions or fines for multiple Argentine players and coaching staff. Some commentators have called for Argentina to be banned from the 2030 World Cup, though individual sanctions are considered more likely.

Argentina drew additional criticism for turning their backs on Spain during the post-match ceremony and bypassing the mixed zone, violating their media obligations under tournament rules.

Gavi Urges Forgiveness

In a surprising turn, Gavi — one of the primary targets of the Argentine aggression — called for restraint rather than punishment.

"I don't think they should be sanctioned. I understand it's not a good image for the younger players, but football also has that violent side. In the end, it's all football."

— Gavi, Spain midfielder

Paredes broke his silence on social media but made no mention of the brawl. "Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves — but with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had," he wrote.

What Comes Next

FIFA's disciplinary committee will review the prosecutor's findings before issuing any sanctions. The investigation is expected to examine video evidence and match officials' reports from the final. Individual bans could affect players' availability for upcoming international fixtures, including the 2026-27 Nations League and World Cup 2030 qualifying campaigns.

Dani Olmo offered Spain's definitive response to the fracas. "What's important are the values you want to transmit," the midfielder told reporters. "We are an example for many generations, and I think they should be too."
